app.title: Protein Cleaver
app.summary: A person pastes a protein sequence or fetches one by accession number, then picks the proteases, the missed cleavages allowed, length and mass limits, and any fixed modifications. The interface digests the sequence in silico. It lists every resulting peptide with its mass, and can also add inferred charge and m/z and model-predicted retention time, ion mobility and detectability. It then shows where the cleavage sites fall, how much of the sequence the peptides cover and how coverage changes as each limit loosens. A motif search counts pattern matches in each peptide and colours how well the motif sites are covered.

task.text: Predict which peptides a protease digest of a protein will give, with their properties, and how much of the protein those peptides cover.

data.text: One protein sequence, optionally with modifications written in the sequence, cut into a table of peptides. Each peptide is a span of the sequence with computed and predicted properties.
data.item: a peptide: a stretch of the protein sequence between cleavage sites

stage.text: planning a protease digest and choosing target peptides before a mass spectrometry run

mechanism.text: Every option in the sidebar feeds one digest that reruns on each change. Tabs then show the peptide table with summary counts, the sequence drawn residue by residue with cleavage sites and coverage colours, coverage curves against each limit, and a motif search that recolours coverage and counts matches per peptide.

field.text: in-silico protein digestion for bottom-up mass spectrometry proteomics

workflow.name: split a sequence at rule-defined sites into fragments, filter them by their properties and measure how much of the sequence they cover

steps.here: Paste a ProForma sequence into the text area, or type an accession number and press Fetch from UniProt. A sample protein is loaded at start.

steps.step: set the rules that cut the sequence and the limits on the pieces
steps.here: Choose proteases from a list, add an optional custom cleavage regex, and set the maximum missed cleavages, semi-enzymatic, min/max length and min/max neutral mass (monoisotopic or average). Fixed, N-terminal and C-terminal modifications go in an editable table.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Optional checkboxes infer charge from the K/R count to give m/z windows, and predict retention time, ion mobility and a proteotypic score with bundled models. Thresholds can drop peptides with invalid retention times or non-proteotypic peptides.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The Peptides tab shows counts of total, semi, enzymatic and unique peptides, and a sortable table with start, end, missed cleavages, mass, charge, m/z, RT, IM and a score. Each row links to a fragment-ion viewer.

steps.step: see how much of the sequence the pieces cover
steps.here: The Cleavage & Coverage tab lists the site indexes, marks each cut in the sequence with %, and colours each residue by how many peptides cover it, with the count on hover and a colour bar. Line charts show coverage against max missed cleavages, peptide length and peptide mass.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: The Motif Analysis tab takes a regex, counts the matches in each peptide, marks uncovered motif residues in red, colours the covered ones, and lists the peptides with their motif counts.

distinctive: Several proteases plus a custom cleavage regex combine into one set of cleavage sites, with missed cleavages and semi-specific cuts allowed
Coverage is recomputed at every setting of each limit, so the person sees what loosening missed cleavages, length or mass would gain
Pretrained models predict retention time, ion mobility and detectability for each peptide, and can filter the list on them
Modifications can be written inline in the sequence or applied as fixed and terminal mass shifts, and they change every peptide mass
All settings are kept in the page URL, so a digest can be shared as a link
